rationale: Antiochus writes from the islands before the later notice that he has entered his ancestral land to claim the kingdom.
Tryphon now loses his troops, contrasting with his earlier rise when the forces dismissed by Demetrius joined the young Antiochus he supported; the passages describe different changes of allegiance.
Tryphon's flight by ship continues his earlier retreat to Dora and escape from the land-and-sea siege described there.
